definition: Automatic summarization is the process of shortening a set of data computationally, to create a subset (a summary) that represents the most important or relevant information within the original content.
details: Artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms are commonly developed and employed to achieve this, specialized for different types of data. Text summarization is usually implemented by natural language processing methods, designed to locate the most informative sentences in a given document. On the other hand, visual content can be summarized using computer vision algorithms. Image summarization is the subject of ongoing research; existing approaches typically attempt to display the most representative images from a given image collection, or generate a video that only includes the most important content from the entire collection. Video summarization algorithms identify and extract from the original video content the most important frames (key-frames), and/or the most important video segments (key-shots), normally in a temporally ordered fashion. Video summaries simply retain a carefully selected subset of the original video frames and, therefore, are not identical to the output of video synopsis algorithms, where new video frames are being synthesized based on the original video content.

explainer.lead: Automatic summarization uses computation to turn a larger body of content into a shorter version that preserves its most important or relevant information. It can help people grasp the essentials of text, images, or video without going through everything.

tiers.eli5: Imagine reading a long story and telling a friend only the parts they need to know. Automatic summarization teaches a computer to do something similar with documents, picture collections, or videos. The result is shorter, but it should still represent the original content well.
tiers.practitioner: Text summarization commonly uses natural language processing to locate informative sentences, while visual summarization uses computer vision. Image systems may select representative images or generate a video from important collection content; video systems extract key-frames or key-shots, usually in temporal order. A video summary should not be confused with video synopsis, which synthesizes new frames.
tiers.paperLevel: Given original data D, automatic summarization computes a summary S, a subset of D, that represents its most important or relevant information. Methods are specialized by data type, including informative-sentence selection for text and representative-image, key-frame, or key-shot selection for visual content. Image summarization remains an ongoing research area, and selected-frame video summaries differ from video synopsis outputs containing synthesized frames.

explainer.example: For a 30-page report, a text summarizer could identify the sentences containing its main findings and present those selected sentences as a much shorter summary.

usedIn.name: Text summarization
usedIn.detail: Natural language processing methods identify informative sentences in a document.

usedIn.name: Image collection summarization
usedIn.detail: Computer vision approaches display representative images or generate a video containing important collection content.

usedIn.name: Video summarization
usedIn.detail: Algorithms extract important key-frames or key-shots, normally preserving temporal order.

explainer.intuition: A good automatic summary acts like a careful selection: it keeps a small part of the original content while retaining what matters most. The selection method depends on whether the content is text, images, or video.
howItWorks: Provide the original text, image collection, or video.
Apply a method specialized for that data type.
Identify informative sentences, representative images, key-frames, or key-shots.
Retain the selected content, keeping video selections temporally ordered when appropriate.
Return the shorter selection as the summary.
explainer.whyItMatters: It offers a way to represent large amounts of content with a smaller, carefully chosen subset. This can make the essential information easier to access across documents, image collections, and videos.
misconceptions: It is not limited to text: image and video content can also be summarized.
A video summary is not video synopsis; the former selects original frames, while the latter synthesizes new ones.
Image summarization is not a settled problem and remains an ongoing research subject.

diagram.caption: Automatic summarization selects important content using a method suited to the data type.
